Forgive me, I will make up for my fault.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'everything', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: I know everything in my hotel.

meanings.note: polite to one person, or to several people

meanings.en: other forms: вас (gen/acc), вам (dat), вами (instr), вас (prep)
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'you (polite or plural)' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.

meanings.note: Prefix 'до-' marks reaching a boundary or finishing the remainder of an action (stem 'вести'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to drive to'.

examples.trans: Nastya, you will drive me crazy one of these days!

meanings.note: medical practitioner; often used as form of address

examples.trans: Doctor, I urgently need a cast.
It hurts, it hurts! It hurts very much, Doctor!

examples.text: Я умоляю вас, доктор! Это всё ради любви!
examples.trans: I beg you, Doctor! This is all for love!

meanings.note: not to be confused with есть 'there is' (from быть)

examples.text: Я вчера ел маринованные грибы. Может, один гриб был плохой.
examples.trans: Yesterday I ate pickled mushrooms. Maybe one mushroom was bad.

Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to wait, to expect', paired with 'подождать'.

examples.trans: So I shouldn't wait for you tonight?

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'life' in everyday Russian.
Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'втра').

examples.text: Позвони мне вечером. Договоримся на завтра.
examples.trans: Call me this evening. We'll arrange something for tomorrow.

meanings.note: mostly in set phrases: иметь совесть, иметь право = to have the right; everyday 'I have' is у меня есть

examples.trans: You have the right to remain silent.

examples.text: Нина, имей совесть! Я вчера ради вас всё сделал.
examples.trans: Nina, have a heart! Yesterday I did everything for you.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'heart attack' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Это уже второй инфаркт за день.
examples.trans: This is already the second heart attack today.

examples.text: От таких новостей у шефа будет второй инфаркт за день.
examples.trans: From news like that, the chef will have a second heart attack today.

examples.text: Врачи сказали, что нужно беречь сердце от инфаркта.
examples.trans: The doctors said that one must protect the heart from a heart attack.

meanings.en: by the way, speaking of which
meanings.note: Used as a parenthetical word. Core Russian adv meaning 'by the way; handy' in everyday speech.
Это очень кстати. Core Russian adv meaning 'by the way; handy' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Oh, by the way, I almost forgot.

examples.text: Кстати, если хочешь, иди к нам в команду. Шансы у нас огромные.
examples.trans: By the way, if you want, join our team. Our chances are huge.

meanings.note: Diminutive of кусок. Common masculine noun meaning 'slice, little piece, bit' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Можно ещё кусочек? И шампанское можно выпить?
examples.trans: May I have another slice? And can I drink the champagne?

meanings.en: it is necessary, one needs to
meanings.note: + dative of the person + infinitive: мне нужно позвонить

examples.trans: I need to make a call.

examples.text: Мне нужно позвонить губернатору. Дай телефон.
examples.trans: I need to call the governor. Give me a phone.

meanings.note: Prefix 'об-' ('around, about') marks encirclement or comprehensive action (stem 'следование'). Verbal action/result neuter noun formed with '-ение'/'-ание'. Common neuter noun meaning 'medical examination' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Результаты обследования показали, что уровень тоже низкий.
examples.trans: The examination results showed that the level is also low.

examples.text: На кухне ресторана всегда есть обследование.
examples.trans: In the restaurant kitchen there is always medical examination.

meanings.note: Descriptive Russian adjective meaning 'medical', agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Нужно пройти обследование через два дня.
examples.trans: We need to take a medical check-up in two days.

examples.text: А ты обследование прошла или нет?
examples.trans: Wait, did you take your medical check-up or not?

meanings.note: accusative/genitive его (него after prepositions), dative ему (нему)
For masculine and neuter things. Core Russian pron meaning 'he; it' in everyday speech.

meanings.en: other forms: его (gen/acc), ему (dat), им (instr), нём (prep)
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'he; it' in everyday speech.
Declinable neuter noun meaning 'bet', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: Впрочем, как и всегда, я выиграл пари!
examples.trans: As always, I won the bet!

examples.text: Я выиграл пари и доказал свою правоту.
examples.trans: I won the bet and proved I was right.

meanings.note: Prefix 'пере-' denotes crossing over, repeating, or exceeding a limit (stem 'едание'). Verbal action/result neuter noun formed with '-ение'/'-ание'. Common neuter noun meaning 'overeating' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: A common case, overeating is to blame for everything.

examples.text: На кухне отеля всегда есть переедание.
examples.trans: In the hotel kitchen there is always overeating.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'беда'). Common feminine noun meaning 'victory, triumph' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Люди в городе аплодируют вашей победе!
examples.trans: People in the town are applauding your victory!

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'казать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to show', paired with 'показывать'.

examples.trans: Shall we show this to Anikeev?

examples.text: Ну, покажите руки. Что у вас за спиной?
examples.trans: Well, show me your hands. What is behind your back?

meanings.note: Последний раз = for the last time. Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'следний'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('last, final').

examples.trans: I'm asking for the last time.
I'm asking for the last time. Where is the money?

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'district prefect' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Today the prefect will be at the grand opening.
Right now the prefect will cut our ribbon.

meanings.note: = Enjoy your meal!. Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'ятный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('pleasant, nice').

examples.trans: Very well! Have a pleasant evening.

meanings.en: to continue, last, remain in progress
meanings.note: Intransitive imperfective verb. Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'должаться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to continue, go on, last', paired with 'продолжиться'.

examples.trans: Calm down, the special operation continues.

meanings.note: + genitive. Core Russian prep meaning 'for the sake of' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Work, work. It's all for us.

meanings.note: Prefix 'рас-' ('apart, un-, thoroughly') indicates distribution or intensive action (stem 'пространённый'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('common / widespread').

examples.trans: A common case, overeating is to blame for everything.

examples.text: Шеф говорит, что это очень распространённый выбор.
examples.trans: The chef says that this is a very common choice.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'record' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Кто съест антрекот, может за него не платить.
examples.trans: Whoever eats the entrecote does not have to pay for it.

examples.text: Но если я приведу человека, который съест твой антрекот.
examples.trans: But if I bring a person who eats your entrecote.
The prefect ordered the promotional entrecote.

рисковать.gloss: to risk, to take a risk

meanings.en: to risk, to take a risk
meanings.note: чем я рискую? = what have I got to lose?

examples.trans: What have I got to lose?
There's no need to take risks.

examples.text: Бред какой-то. Но, с другой стороны, чем я рискую?
examples.trans: What nonsense. But on the other hand, what have I got to lose?

meanings.note: + instrumental; со before some consonant clusters: со всеми

examples.trans: Share it all equally with everyone, understand?

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'держивать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to restrain / hold back'.

examples.text: Надо всё сделать и сдерживать вовремя.
examples.trans: We need to do everything and to restrain on time.

meanings.note: Reflexive; no nominative. Core Russian pron meaning 'oneself' in everyday speech.

examples.text: А с Пашей я снова чувствую себя женщиной.
examples.trans: And with Pasha I feel like a woman again.

meanings.note: На случай, если... = in case. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'лучай'). Common masculine noun meaning 'case, occasion, incident' in everyday Russian.
Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'лучай'). Common masculine noun meaning 'case, occasion, incident' in everyday Russian.
На всякий случай = just in case. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'лучай'). Common masculine noun meaning 'case, occasion, incident' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Возьмите, пожалуйста. На случай, если передумаете.
examples.trans: Please take this. In case you change your mind.

meanings.note: Core Russian adv meaning 'too, also' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Мы же здесь выросли. И о людях тоже надо думать.
examples.trans: After all, we grew up here. And you have to think about people too.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.
Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Я точно не помню его адрес.
examples.trans: I don't remember his exact address.

examples.text: Точно, полиция была! А что с машиной?
examples.trans: That's right, the police were there! And what about the car?

meanings.note: Relational adjective formed with the Slavic suffix '-ский' ('pertaining to'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('human, presentable, decent').

examples.trans: To bring into a presentable state.

examples.text: Нужно срочно привести его в человеческий вид!
examples.trans: He must urgently be brought into a presentable state!

Conjunction. Core Russian pron meaning 'what' in everyday speech.
Core Russian pron meaning 'what' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

points at something: это моё = that's mine
Linking word: главное — это народ. Core Russian pron meaning 'this, that; it is' in everyday speech.

meanings.en: other forms: этого, этому, это, этим, этом
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'this, that; it is' in everyday speech.
